forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Stroud council owed £100.717m at 30 June 2026; its next loan repayment, £6m, falls due in March 2032
news_drafts.lead:
Stroud District Council had £100.717m of external borrowing at 30 June 2026, the end of the first quarter of its financial year. The next loan it must repay, £6m, is not due until March 2032, more than five years after the date of the figures. They come from the quarter's treasury management report (how a council borrows, invests its spare cash and manages the risks of both), which went to the Audit and Standards Committee on 29 September.

The council also intends to use internal borrowing of £36.690m to pay for its capital programme, its planned spending on long-lasting assets such as buildings, roads and equipment. Internal borrowing means paying for that spending from the council's own money put aside, rather than taking out a loan. That saves interest but uses up some of the cushion.

The report sets out the council's borrowing position in a table and states the March 2032 repayment as the next on its schedule.

findings.paper_title: Audit & Standards Performance Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Revenues and Benefits system cloud migration planned for November 2026 delivery
findings.detail: The council has initiated a Revenues and Benefits Project to move its systems to a cloud-based platform, with delivery targeted for November 2026 as part of LGR preparation.
findings.matters: System readiness is critical for operational continuity during LGR transition; peers managing the same merger would want visibility of implementation timelines for equivalent systems
findings.quote: Revenues and Benefits Project (cloud move) has been kicked off and plan is to deliver in November 2026

findings.paper_title: Audit & Standards Performance Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Data intelligence work for local government reorganization shows 0% progress with October and December 2026 deadlines
findings.detail: Two implementation sub-actions under the Data and Intelligence Strategy are showing zero progress, despite deadlines in October and December 2026. These activities are intended to prepare the council for local government reorganization. While earlier design and approval phases were completed, implementation has not yet started.
findings.matters: For finance officers at peer councils preparing for LGR, understanding the pace and status of preparatory work—particularly data systems and intelligence—directly informs their own planning and risk assessment
findings.figures: 0% progress on both sub-actions; due dates 31-Oct-2026 and 31-Dec-2026
findings.quote: Develop improved internal resources for data intelligence to support preparation for LGR benchmarking and data analysis. 31-Dec-2026  0%

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Revised Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: HRA 30-year Business Plan is in development and not yet approved; control marked Not Effective
findings.detail: The control for maintaining an HRA 30-year Business Plan to ensure the HRA balances is marked as Not Effective. The plan is in development and due for approval at the December 2026 Housing Committee meeting. Until this plan is approved, the council cannot provide assurance over the Housing Revenue Account's long-term financial sustainability.
findings.matters: The HRA Business Plan is a key governance document assuring lenders and the finance director about the council's ability to manage housing operations sustainably; its absence until December represents a gap in assurance over a significant reserve fund.
findings.quote: 30 year Business Plan is in development and due for approval at December 2026 Housing Committee

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Revised Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: Savings targets for 2026/27 have not yet been identified and control is marked Not Effective
findings.detail: The mitigation for delivery of savings targets identified in the MTFP is marked as Not Effective, with the note that work remains to be undertaken to identify and deliver savings during 2026/27 and ongoing. This represents a gap in financial planning mid-way through the budget setting cycle, with no clarity yet on how the council will balance its finances for the coming year.
findings.matters: A lender would be concerned that savings are not yet identified this late in the budget cycle, indicating potential unresolved financial pressures or delayed decisions on how the council will achieve required savings.
findings.figures: 2026/27 budget year; status as of August 2026
findings.quote: Work to be undertaken to identify and deliver savings during 2026/27 and ongoing

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Revised Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation risk score increased from 9 to 12 following MHCLG pause announcement on 7 September
findings.detail: The likelihood component of the LGR risk has been increased from 3 to 4 due to uncertainty following MHCLG's announcement that Local Government Reorganisation will be paused for a review. This creates uncertainty about the review's duration and whether LGR will proceed in Gloucestershire at all. The council indicates the risk profile will be updated once more information emerges about the review's outcome.
findings.matters: A pause in LGR creates material organisational and financial planning uncertainty at a time when the council is managing multiple pressures, and lenders would be concerned about this shift from lower to higher risk of service and structural disruption.
findings.figures: Risk score increased from 9 to 12; likelihood component increased from 3 to 4
findings.quote: The probability/likelihood has been increased from 3 to 4 following the announcement from MHCLG on 7 September that Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) will be paused for a review.
